rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for something considered as one complete thing rather than as separate parts.

example.english: The whole painting is beautiful overall.
example.jyutping: seng4 fuk1 waa6 ge3 zing2 tai2 hou2 leng3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice: use 成 for an undivided item, and before a large quantity it means “a whole lot” or “a whole bunch.”

example.english: I waited for you the whole afternoon.
example.traditional: 我成個下晝都喺度等你。
example.jyutping: ngo5 sing4 go3 haa6 zau3 dou1 hai2 dou6 dang2 nei5

rows.note: Use 健全 for a person’s body or mind when it is sound, intact, and functioning normally.

example.english: His mind is still whole after the stroke.
example.traditional: 佢中風之後，個腦仲算健全。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zung1 fung1 zi1 hau6 go3 nou5 zung6 syun3 gin6 cyun4

rows.note: Use 全麥 specifically for whole-wheat or whole-grain wheat products rather than refined wheat products.

example.english: I eat whole-wheat bread every morning.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ziu1 ziu1 dou1 sik6 cyun4 mak6 min6 baau1

rows.note: Use 全脂 for milk or other dairy products from which the fat has not been removed.

example.english: Would whole milk be better for children?
example.traditional: 小朋友飲全脂奶會唔會好啲？
example.jyutping: siu2 pang4 jau5 jam2 cyun4 zi1 naai5 wui5 m4 wui5 hou2 di1
